title: Thrust vs. weight
about: How a car can fly: Newton's 3rd Law and the thrust-to-weight ratio.

html: To fly, push air down hard enough that the air pushes you up.
That's Newton's 3rd Law: every push has an equal push back. Let go of a blown-up balloon and it shoots away as the air rushes out.
The flying car shown in October 2026 used compressed-air thrusters: tanks of squeezed air blasting out of nozzles.
Weight is how hard gravity pulls: mass × 9.8. A 1,000 kg car weighs about 9.8 kN (kilonewtons).

• Above 1.0: the thrusters can lift the car by themselves.
  • Below 1.0: they can only slow its fall.

steps.q: A car weighs 12 kN. Its nozzles push with 9 kN. Can the thrusters lift it by themselves?

options: Switch from a steel body to carbon fiber
steps.explain: Carbon fiber is much lighter than steel. Same thrust, less weight, so the ratio goes up.
